title: Add a reversible philosophy inquiry application profile
objective: Add an argument-agnostic, application-level philosophy inquiry bundle validator, disclosure-safe projector, deterministic Markdown/JSON renderer, branch comparison, and read-only adapter without changing normative protocol semantics or accepted public knowledge.
required_evaluation: fictional fixtures covering referential closure, content identities, argument/source distinctions, evaluation frontiers, branch diffs, and private/public noninterference
tests proving reordered and duplicate imports produce the same content-addressed projection
tests proving private mutations cannot affect any public count, text, topology, ordering, or manifest digest
full deterministic make check and changed-path audit
acceptance: a strict application-level philosophy inquiry bundle distinguishes propositions from assertions, premise roles from textual evidence, source works from snapshots and spans, inferential support from evidential support, and policy-relative evaluation from truth
the importer fails closed on unknown references, hash mismatches, duplicate conflicting identities, and forbidden intrinsic truth or confidence fields
private and disclosure-safe public dossiers compile deterministically to Markdown and JSON twins from the same validated bundle
branch comparison exposes added, removed, and revised claims, changed inference edges, concessions, scope changes, sources, objections, replies, and manuscript consequences
the generic implementation and fixtures contain no unpublished competition content, private logs, rankings, selections, prompts, manuscripts, or private-state-revealing hashes
the change stops at a draft pull request and does not merge, deploy, publish a release, admit knowledge, or alter normative authority
limitations: The profile is a reversible application contract, not an Epistemic Mesh protocol standard.
The bounded task exposes Python read adapters; integrating new public CLI, REST, or MCP routes requires a separate contract because those paths are intentionally forbidden here.
Fictional fixtures prove software behavior, not the truth or originality of any philosophical argument.
